beforeRows.summary: If a tutor calls off or is absent, reassignStudentsFromAbsentTutor redistributes their students, and a lead-capable regular tutor is promoted to LEAD automatically; integrateJoiningTutor absorbs a tutor who joins late.
Each session record carries its videoconference URL and Zoom host key; Videoconf entities later match videoconference attendance back to the session.

Automatic tiering: non-lead tutors fill before the lead, each up to baseLoad = floor(students/tutors), then overflow. Within a tier the algorithm prefers lowest current load, then highest prior history with the student (continuity fast-path), then a balanced proficiency mix; emergency round-robin as fallback.

The Dev Team builds these surfaces and the Design Team draws them, working from what the research team finds. They support this scenario throughout — this cell stands for the whole of it rather than repeating on every step.

beforeRows.content: Turns on the projector or interactive whiteboard.
beforeRows.summary: The classroom-side counterpart to tutors opening the session in the app: the teacher's own display has to be live before anything shown from the PLUS App or Zoom is visible to the room.
Lead opens the session detail page in the PLUS App to review the roster and tutor list before start. Sessions are only joinable from the app within 15 minutes of start time (Join Session gate).

This is the tutor's first read of who they're paired with and whether the Zoom link is live; the Join Session button only unlocks within 15 minutes of start, so opening early shows the roster but nothing to click yet.
Session detail page: roster, assigned tutors, Zoom link, and Join Session button (enabled within 15 minutes of start).

beforeRows.content: Tutor supervisor team sets up session details.
beforeRows.summary: Supervisors edit, cancel, or revert sessions from the Sessions admin (scopes: single / recurring / date range). There is no in-app session creation — session records arrive via DB import at semester setup.

The Dev Team builds these surfaces and the Design Team draws them, working from what the research team finds. They support this scenario throughout — this cell stands for the whole of it rather than repeating on every step.

beforeRows.content: Opens the slide deck shared by the tutor team.
beforeRows.summary: The one piece of tutor-side prep the teacher directly acts on: displaying the shared deck on the classroom's own screen. It is the teacher's half of a session opening that otherwise happens entirely inside Zoom.

The lead is first into the room, ahead of tutors and the teacher, so the session exists on Zoom before anyone else needs it. Breakout rooms, attendance, and the shared slide deck all depend on this happening first.
The tutor's entry point into the session; attendance, breakout placement, and screen sharing later in the row all assume this join already happened.
Tutors join the session via Zoom.

beforeRows.content: Tutor supervisor team sets up Zoom link.
beforeRows.summary: The Zoom link the supervisor team sets here is what the whole room depends on a step later - tutors, the lead tutor, and the teacher all join through it, so a wrong or missing link stalls the session before it starts.
Dev Team builds the app and the Design Team creates the screens and flows relevant to this step. Both implement the findings from the research team into the app in their respective role.

beforeRows.content: Posts the session link in the school's learning platform or shares the QR code, depending on session needs.
beforeRows.summary: The teacher is the one who actually gets students into Zoom, posting the link where the school already expects it, or a QR code when that is easier. Nothing the lead does inside the app substitutes for this; it is the only path most students have into the session.

Lead marks which tutors have arrived. In 2026 production data, 83.4% of rostered students end up with an attendance record but only 31.8% of sessions are fully covered — the roster check here is the first defense.

beforeRows.content: Signs in with the lead tutor and confirms co-host permissions.
beforeRows.summary: Co-host is required to self-move between breakout rooms. Note: any co-host can move students, which is one source of attendance drift when moves happen outside the assignment list.
Tutors sign in for the session via Zoom.

The one piece of session readiness that belongs to the teacher alone: a classroom network the tutors have no way to check or fix from inside Zoom. If it fails, no breakout room the lead builds will hold a connection.
Lead creates breakout rooms in Zoom using the breakout calculator from training, grants co-host to regular tutors, and starts the recording. Rooms are visited sequentially per tutor.
Lead tutors create breakout rooms on Zoom.

beforeRows.content: Makes sure all student devices are ready.
beforeRows.summary: Physical-room readiness, chargers, logins, seats, that only the teacher can confirm, running alongside the lead and tutors' own review of the dashboard's room order. Neither side can see the other's checklist.

beforeRows.content: Reminds tutors to go through rooms in the order of the dashboard list.
beforeRows.summary: Keeps tutors working the PLUS App's dashboard order rather than an ad hoc one, so the room-by-room sequence tutors actually follow matches what the app and researchers expect. It is a procedural nudge, not a permission: any tutor could read the same list.

beforeRows.content: Reviews the student list for the session.
beforeRows.summary: The tutor previews their own student list before the room-order sequence starts, so they know who they're seeing rather than discovering it live as rooms open.
Lead tutors connect with regular tutors on Zoom about the student list.
Dev Team builds the app and the Design Team creates the screens and flows relevant to this step. Both implement the findings from the research team into the app in their respective role.

beforeRows.content: Reminds students to plug in their headphones and use their real names in the session.
beforeRows.summary: Two small habits the teacher enforces before tutors ever see a student: real names, so the lead's roster-matching later actually works, and headphones, so breakout-room audio does not bleed across the physical classroom.

beforeRows.content: Gives the breakout room list to the tutors.
beforeRows.summary: The app's assignment list is the source of truth, but distribution is manual today: the lead relays each tutor's student list via Zoom chat or Slack DM. Tutors then hunt for matching names in the Zoom participant list.

beforeRows.content: Receives the breakout room list from the lead tutor.

Lead tutors connect with regular tutors about assigned breakout rooms via Zoom.
The tutor connects with student via Zoom in individual breakout room.
